purpose: Portable excerpts supporting Jeep diligence J02 and J22. Exact upstream authored fields are preserved; they are reused research, not independent new observations. Original public source URLs and limitations remain in each excerpt.

excerpt.question: What changed around Q2 2024 that disproportionately hurt US Grand Cherokee 4xe sales, and what does that imply for sustainable retail recovery?
excerpt.units: US vehicles reported sold, calendar quarters; not shipments, North American revenue or retail-only registrations.

annual_decomposition.limit: Arithmetic allocation, not causal attribution or revenue contribution.

channel_check.interpretation: With consistent channel definitions, fleet must fall because total falls while retail rises. No absolute retail base or 4xe channel allocation disclosed.

q4_channel_followup_2026_10_13.fleet_identity: Delta fleet = -6514 - Delta retail. Positive retail growth requires fleet contraction greater than 6514 vehicles, assuming comparable populations and classification.
q4_channel_followup_2026_10_13.limit: No absolute retail base, 4xe channel split, or inference of consumer substitution.
q4_channel_followup_2026_10_13.novelty: Previously held release, retail bullet newly incorporated. See normalization-mechanism-gap-audit.json.

model_status.ready: Quarterly and half-year variant unit decomposition; distinguish recovery of non4xe from rebound of entire brand or PHEV.
model_status.not_ready: Causal weights, retail-only elasticity, or recovery forecast assuming return of all lost4xe units.
model_status.decision: Do not label the entire year as uniform Grand Cherokee demand collapse or assume launch/production repair alone restores demand.
recovery_tests: If retail non4xe already displaced4xe, adding all lost4xe units to a recovery scenario double-counts customers.
Recoverable supply blockage requires evidence of unsatisfied demand at viable price once units become sellable.
Incentive-dependent volume must be evaluated alongside manufacturer/dealer margin and residual support.

sales23.limitation: US retail plus fleet; cannot infer household demand from totals.

excerpt.question: Does household-demand evidence support persistent brand inferiority or a subsequent loss of relative value?
excerpt.price_definition: KBB US manufacturer-group average transaction prices exclude applied consumer incentives. Mix varies across groups and periods. December 2019 is context, not a seasonally matched comparison.

observations.finding: KBB Q4 2019 Ram 1500 shopping +32% QoQ; Grand Cherokee consideration +33%; both top-ten most-shopped non-luxury vehicles. Ram first on six of twelve perception factors. Survey and shopping evidence, not willingness-to-pay or population-wide brand preference.
March 2023 to March 2024 Stellantis-versus-Ford average price gap shifted from -451 to +3991 dollars: +4442. Mix and incentives prevent like-for-like overpricing interpretation.
December 2024 Jeep ATP -6.3% YoY; Ram -1.6%; Ram incentives over 13% of ATP. This is a monthly snapshot.
Q2 2025 Ram 1500 retail +68% YoY, total +17%; Grand Cherokee retail +5%. Company-wide total US sales still -10%. Low base, supply recovery, offers and mix confound attribution.
H2 2024 Grand Cherokee non-4xe sales +9.78%, 4xe -69.42%. Retail plus fleet. Inconsistent with uniform nameplate rejection; not proof of financing causality.

excerpt.judgment: Blanket always-second-tier hypothesis is too broad. Relative price/product mismatch is plausible and directionally supported; an enduring household customer base existed for major models, but sustainable profitable recovery remains unproven.
excerpt.model_use: Use verified actual sales and price observations descriptively. Do not fit elasticity, causal contribution weights or recoverable-volume forecast from these aggregates.

cases.classification: Strong volume recovery; long-run profitability not established
cases.launch: Redesign of existing nameplate, spring 2023 US launch, MY2024
cases.price_basis: Launch MSRP including destination; not net transaction
cases.product: More room and standard safety/technology at low starting price; all five trim starting prices below25000. Old/new sales comparison confounded by supply and transition.
cases.advertising: April2023 Lead Dream Chaser social promotion; aspirations and accessible lifestyle. Not a complete advertising inventory.
cases.support: GM Q12024: incentive estimate about95% below small-SUV segment average. Point-in-time management claim, not annual audited cost.
cases.mechanism: Practical offering at affordable entry price; production ramp and fuller-year exposure contribute.
cases.disconfirm: Without ad reach and comparable supply, cannot assign growth to advertising or product changes alone.

cases.classification: Strong launch growth; durability/profitability not established
cases.price_basis: Launch MSRP including destination; not net transaction
cases.product: Design and cabin presentation at accessible price; FWD turbo three-cylinder rather than high-performance AWD proposition.
cases.advertising: Exceptional by design launchedFeb27 2024; brand-level digital video and owned channels, not Envista-only spending.
cases.support: GM Q12024: incentives about85% below segment average; management claim.
cases.mechanism: Low entry price plus styling; first full year materially boosts annual comparison.
cases.disconfirm: Named2024campaign postdates2023sales; cannot explain initial adoption. New-to-Buick is not necessarily conquest from other OEMs.

limitations: Purposive four-case study, not representative matched sample. Two successful GM small SUVs are related product programs, not independent experiments; Ram is a mechanism case in another segment.
Calendar Q4 comparisons reduce partial-year distortion for three2023launches but do not align exact months since launch or remove supply ramps. No complete monthly launch-age panel.
New-car total sales include fleet, and dealer listings are proxies; no uniform consumer-only panel.
No comparable campaign spending, reach, brand lift, lead conversion or incremental sales data. Presence of a campaign does not establish equal ad intensity or effectiveness.

forecast_rules.forecast_condition: Model fills a price/use-case gap and can be supplied in meaningful affordable configurations.
forecast_rules.require: Net payments, actual trim availability and several quarters of sell-through; deduct cannibalization.

forecast_rules.forecast_condition: High stock persists despite availability and substantial marketing.
forecast_rules.require: Test price/payment, practical features and cross-shopping; no automatic rebound on ad launch.

forecast_rules.forecast_condition: Wanted variants were unavailable and become consistently deliverable.
forecast_rules.require: Sales improve with stock normalization; distinguish pipeline refill from customer demand.

forecast_rules.forecast_condition: Exposure changes precede qualified interest and purchases after price/stock controls.
forecast_rules.require: Incremental lift or comparable geography/time variation. Without it, no separate numerical ad uplift.
